source_review.notes: Checked the primary Chandy-Lamport distributed-snapshot paper; current or explicitly versioned official Apache Flink fault-tolerance, state, checkpointing, monitoring, and savepoint documentation; current Apache Spark Structured Streaming checkpoint/state documentation; current Apache Kafka Streams restoration and state-store documentation; the RocksDB checkpoint documentation; and Google Cloud Dataflow exactly-once guidance. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Runtime-specific semantics are attributed.

evidence: Reviewed checkpoint tuple C_k, source/operator/channel/coordinator/sink/digest components, checkpoint IDs, state handles, byte categories, checkpoint times, replay distance, incremental dependency graph, and RPO/RTO notation.
Checked consistent-cut, completion, compatibility, restore-selection, and replay predicates with explicit scopes and units.
Checked that working state, durable checkpoint storage, local recovery copies, automatic checkpoints, externalized checkpoints, and savepoints remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The model treats checkpoint completion, integrity, compatibility, and recoverability as separate predicates rather than inferring them from file presence.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced selected checkpoint 40, source offset 1200, state size 640 MiB, replay distance 350, and rejection reasons for checkpoints 41 through 43.
Recomputed replay distance as 1550 - 1200 = 350 records and verified the selection scan rejects incomplete, incompatible, and missing-handle candidates before choosing the newest admissible point.
Checked the 12 GiB unaligned-channel example, shared-base retention example, and 99-of-100 acknowledgement example preserve their stated units and completion implications.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No universal checkpoint interval, timeout, concurrency, state-size, replay-distance, retention count, RPO, or RTO threshold is prescribed.

evidence: Verified aligned barriers exclude overtaking post-barrier records while unaligned checkpoints account for required in-flight records in channel state.
Verified atomic completion makes pre-publication partial state unselectable and post-publication state a durable recovery root under the stated durability assumptions.
Verified restore equivalence pairs all checkpoint components from one epoch with source replay, and reference-counted incremental retention preserves every live transitive dependency.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: End-to-end exactly-once remains conditional on deterministic processing plus transactional or idempotent external-effect handling.

evidence: Reviewed empty and very large state, one and many inputs, skew, sustained backpressure, large channel buffers, concurrent checkpoints, and checkpoint timeouts.

Reviewed crashes during trigger, barrier, snapshot, upload, acknowledgement, completion, notification, and restore; duplicate/lost acknowledgements; partial/corrupt handles; missing incremental bases; and retention gaps.

Reviewed unknown sink outcomes, source-retention loss, topology/serializer/runtime changes, rescaling and key-group redistribution, cleanup races, cancellation, encryption-key expiry, fallback, and rollback.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: A candidate that cannot prove completeness, integrity, compatibility, source availability, and sink resolution is rejected rather than repaired by mixing epochs.

evidence: Traced one checkpoint ID through source positions, operator/keyed state, in-flight channels, coordinator/timers, sink preparations, and compatibility digests.
Checked completion only after all mandatory durable handles, attempt-private partial state, idempotent acknowledgements, aligned/unaligned record accounting, and stable operator/state identities.
Checked source-state pairing, sink transaction identity, key-group mapping, serializer compatibility, shared-dependency reachability, retention leases, and fenced recovery epochs.
invariant_checking.notes: Recovery always selects one completed checkpoint root and never advances offsets independently of the restored state cut.

evidence: Reviewed consistent-cut, atomic-completion, restore-equivalence, and incremental-retention arguments with their reliability, determinism, durability, and compatibility premises.

Checked counterexamples for mixed checkpoint IDs, directory-based completion, omitted channel buffers, lost shared bases, incompatible serializers, stale task messages, and newly identified sink transactions.
Checked fault injection covers each protocol boundary and compares recovered state/output/effects with a reference while measuring fallback and RPO/RTO.
proof_review.notes: Checkpoint success, restore success, state equivalence, sink-effect equivalence, and objective attainment require separate evidence.

evidence: Audited checkpoint, consistent cut, barrier, aligned/unaligned mode, state handle, completion record, restore compatibility, and replay-distance terminology.
Confirmed full, incremental, and changelog state; working state and durable snapshots; and automatic, externalized, and manual recovery points are distinguished.
Confirmed checkpoint duration, restore duration, replay/catch-up time, RPO, RTO, managed-state exactly-once, invocation count, and external-effect semantics are not conflated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Flink, Spark, Kafka Streams, RocksDB, and Dataflow mechanisms are not presented as interchangeable runtime contracts.

evidence: Reviewed trigger/completion/failure/timeout counts, start delay, alignment, synchronous/asynchronous duration, state/channel bytes, throughput, dependency depth, checkpoint age, and replay distance.
Reviewed restore resource wait, download/open/deserialization, channel initialization, source seek, replay, first output, steady progress, sink resolution, fallback count, and achieved RPO/RTO.
Confirmed segmentation by checkpoint mode, backend/storage, operator/subtask, job/graph/code version, input/load cohort, failure domain, and observation window.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: A low checkpoint duration or successful completion is not mislabeled as low restore time, bounded replay, valid compatibility, or end-to-end exactly-once.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed consistent distributed cuts, aligned and unaligned barriers, state handles, full/incremental/changelog snapshots, atomic completion, restore selection, recovery sequencing, compatibility, tuning, retention, security, and verification.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable checkpoint identities and handles, private uploads, durable completion, idempotent acknowledgements, shared-state reference graphs, source/sink reconciliation, stable UIDs, serializer gates, rescaling, cleanup leases, observability, restore drills, and fault injection. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from consistent cuts and barriers through storage/completion to recovery, compatibility, tuning, and operations. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover selection, aligned/unaligned behavior, atomic completion, incremental cleanup, rescaling, serializer evolution, sink ambiguity, and restore drills.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Chandy-Lamport paper author, Flink/Spark/Kafka/RocksDB/Dataflow maintainer, distributed-systems/database/streaming/storage/platform/SRE/security specialist, production workload operator, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
